results.summary_before: This design implements a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron network inspired by snnTorch. It accepts an 8-bit input current split between two input neurons, and each neuron integrates the current, decays its state by bit-shifting each clock cycle, and emits a spike when its state reaches or exceeds a threshold of 8. The network has multiple layers, with spike outputs for each layer and state variable outputs for the output layer neurons. The documentation provides no testing procedure or external hardware requirements, and the design is a compact digital implementation of a spiking neural network building block.

results.summary_before: This design implements a delta recurrent neural network (Delta RNN) combined with a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron. It accepts an 8-bit input current, computes the difference between previous and current states, and generates a spike when that difference exceeds a set delta threshold. Outputs include the state variable and the difference in states. The documentation provides no testing procedure or external hardware requirements, and the design is a compact digital implementation of a spiking neural network component.

results.summary_before: This project implements a small spiking neural network based on the leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron model. It consists of three input neurons that receive 5-bit input currents, and one output neuron that integrates weighted spikes from the input neurons. The design can be tested in simulation or on an FPGA, with LEDs and switches for input and output. It is suitable for basic pattern recognition or response simulations.

results.summary_before: This design is a versatile PWM generator with adjustable frequency and duty cycle. It takes a 6-bit divisor input to set the frequency by dividing the clock, and two control inputs to increase or decrease the duty cycle by 10% steps. The PWM output can be used to drive RGB LEDs, servomotors, and other devices, but external power is recommended for the driven device. The design is intended to be tested by applying a clock, setting the divisor, and adjusting the duty cycle while observing the PWM output.

results.summary_before: This design is a compact 8-bit RISC-V processor core that uses a customized compressed instruction set (RVC) with 16-bit instructions to fit Tiny Tapeout constraints. It includes a control unit, an 8-register file, an ALU, and a single-cycle datapath, and it executes R-Type, I-Type, L-Type, S-Type, and B-Type instructions. Testing is done by setting the instruction on the input pins and clocking once to receive the result on the output pins, with different instruction types producing different outputs. The design is notable for being an educational implementation of a RISC-V core optimized for area, but it lacks detailed documentation on its instruction encoding and limitations.
